question: The procedure for impeachment of the President of India is mentioned in ________ of the Constitution of India. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (25/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: Article 30
Article 77
Article 61
Article 66
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 61

Explanation:
The procedure for impeachment of the President of India is mentioned in Article 61 of the Constitution of India. Impeachment can be initiated only on the ground of violation of the Constitution. The process can be started in either House of Parliament with a resolution signed by one-fourth of its members. The resolution must be passed by a two-thirds majority in both Houses for the President to be removed. A mandatory 14-day notice is required before introducing the impeachment motion. Articles 30, 77, and 66 deal with minority educational institutions, executive business, and Vice-President election respectively.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Ground for impeachment of President → Violation of Constitution
☛ House to initiate impeachment → Either Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha
☛ Majority required for removal → Two-thirds majority
☛ Notice period for impeachment → 14 days
☛ Article related to President impeachment → Article 61

solution:

question: Which one of the following Committees in India is related to Tax reforms? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (25/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: Meera Seth Committee
Ghosh Committee
Raja Chelliah Committee
Anand Sinha Committee
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Raja Chelliah Committee

Explanation:
The Raja Chelliah Committee was constituted in 1991 by the Government of India to recommend tax reforms. Chaired by Dr. Raja J. Chelliah, the committee focused on simplification of direct and indirect taxes, reduction in tax rates, and widening of the tax base. Its recommendations led to comprehensive tax reforms in the 1990s, including reduction in customs and excise duties. While the Meera Seth Committee deals with child labour, the Ghosh Committee deals with banking reforms, and the Anand Sinha Committee is related to the banking sector. The Raja Chelliah Committee remains a landmark in India's tax reform history.

question: Which among the following Articles of the Indian Constitution deals with financial emergency? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (25/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: Article-260
Article-460
Article-360
Article-160
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article-360

Explanation:
Article 360 of the Indian Constitution deals with financial emergency. The President is empowered to proclaim a financial emergency if he is satisfied that the financial stability or credit of India is threatened. During such an emergency, the Central government can interfere in the financial matters of states, such as reducing salaries and allowances of state employees. The proclamation must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within two months. It is one of the three types of emergency powers, the others being national emergency (Article 352) and President's rule in states (Article 356). So far, financial emergency has never been imposed in India.

☛ Article related to Financial Emergency → Article 360
☛ Article related to National Emergency → Article 352
☛ Article related to President's Rule in states → Article 356
☛ Time limit for parliamentary approval after financial emergency proclamation → Two months
☛ Has financial emergency ever been imposed in India → Never
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान के निम्नलिखित अनुच्छेदों में से कौन सा वित्तीय आपातकाल से संबंधित है? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (25/01/2021) Shift 2)

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 360 वित्तीय आपातकाल से संबंधित है। राष्ट्रपति को यह अधिकार है कि यदि वह संतुष्ट हो जाए कि भारत की वित्तीय स्थिरता या साख को खतरा है, तो वह वित्तीय आपातकाल की घोषणा कर सकता है। ऐसी घोषणा के बाद केंद्र सरकार राज्यों के वित्तीय मामलों में हस्तक्षेप कर सकती है, जैसे कि राज्यों के वेतन और भत्तों में कटौती करना। वित्तीय आपातकाल की घोषणा को संसद के दोनों सदनों द्वारा दो महीने के भीतर अनुमोदित किया जाना चाहिए। यह तीन प्रकार की आपातकालीन शक्तियों में से एक है, अन्य दो हैं राष्ट्रीय आपातकाल (अनुच्छेद 352) और राज्यों में राष्ट्रपति शासन (अनुच्छेद 356)। अब तक भारत में कभी भी वित्तीय आपातकाल लागू नहीं किया गया है।

question: Who chaired the commission that drafted the Indian Penal code which was enacted in 1860? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (25/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: Lord Hardinge
Lord Macauly
Lord Linlithgow
Lord Curzon
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lord Macaulay

Explanation:
The Indian Penal Code (IPC) was enacted in 1860. It was drafted by the First Law Commission chaired by Lord Macaulay (Thomas Babington Macaulay). The commission was established in 1833, and the draft was completed in 1837. However, due to various reasons, its implementation was delayed until 1860. The IPC came into effect on 1 January 1862. It is the foundational criminal code of India, largely based on English law principles. Macaulay's draft was comprehensive and served as the basis for criminal law in several other British colonies as well.

☛ Which commission drafted the IPC? → First Law Commission

☛ What was the Act number of IPC? → Act No. 45 of 1860

Explanation:

question: With reference to the Rajya Sabha, which of the following statement is correct? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (25/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: It is a directly elected body like Lok Sabha.
The term of Rajya Sabha is six years.
Rajya Sabha is the lower house of parliament.
The Rajya Sabha is never dissolved.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Rajya Sabha is never dissolved

Explanation:
The Rajya Sabha is the upper house of Parliament and is a permanent house, meaning it is never dissolved. One-third of its members retire every two years. The term of a Rajya Sabha member is six years, but this does not refer to the term of the house. The Rajya Sabha is indirectly elected, unlike the Lok Sabha which is directly elected. The Rajya Sabha cannot be dissolved like the Lok Sabha; it continues indefinitely. According to Article 83, dissolution of the Rajya Sabha is not possible.

Explanation:
राज्य सभा संसद का उच्च सदन है, जो स्थायी सदन है और कभी भंग नहीं होती। इसके एक-तिहाई सदस्य प्रति दो वर्ष में सेवानिवृत्त होते हैं। राज्य सभा के सदस्यों का कार्यकाल छह वर्ष का होता है, लेकिन यह सदन के कार्यकाल को संदर्भित नहीं करता। राज्य सभा अप्रत्यक्ष रूप से निर्वाचित होती है, जबकि लोकसभा प्रत्यक्ष रूप से चुनी जाती है। राज्य सभा लोकसभा की तरह भंग नहीं होती, इसलिए यह एक स्थायी निकाय है। अनुच्छेद 83 के अनुसार, राज्य सभा का विघटन संभव नहीं है।

question: Which of the following features provided by the constitution of India is related to 'Indian Judiciary'? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (25/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: Supremacy of judiciary
Judicial independence
Each state has its own high court
Judges of high courts are elected
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Judicial independence

Explanation:
Judicial independence is a key feature of the Indian Constitution. It ensures that judges can deliver justice without external pressure. Provisions related to the Supreme Court and High Courts are in Part V and Part VI of the Constitution. This independence is vital for democracy as the judiciary reviews the constitutionality of laws. Other options like supremacy of judiciary are not entirely correct because the Constitution is supreme in India.

question: Article 368 of the Indian constitution is related to: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (25/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: amendment of the constitution
election to the post of president
federal feature of our country
national emergency
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is amendment of the constitution

Explanation:
Article 368 of the Indian Constitution deals with the power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and the procedure for doing so. It allows amendments to any part of the Constitution, but certain basic features (like democracy, secularism, federalism) cannot be destroyed, as established by the basic structure doctrine in the Kesavananda Bharati case. An amendment bill must be passed by each house of Parliament with a special majority (2/3 of members present and voting). Some amendments also require ratification by at least half of the state legislatures. As of now, there have been 105 constitutional amendments.

question: The 'right to property' is a: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (27/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: Spiritual right
Legal right
Fundamental right
No right at all
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Legal right

Explanation:
The 'right to property' in the Indian Constitution was originally a fundamental right, but the 44th Amendment (1978) removed it from the list of fundamental rights and placed it under Article 300A, making it a legal right. Now, it is only a constitutional legal right, meaning no person can be deprived of their property except by authority of law. It is no longer enforceable through the Supreme Court directly under fundamental rights. This change was made to balance individual property rights with the state's power of eminent domain for public welfare. Thus, the right to property currently exists as a legal right.

question: Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution makes provision for the division of powers between Union and the States? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (27/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: VII
IV
VIII
III
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is VII

Explanation:
The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution provides for the division of legislative powers between the Union and the States. It contains three lists: the Union List (subjects under the exclusive jurisdiction of the Centre), the State List (subjects under the exclusive jurisdiction of States), and the Concurrent List (subjects on which both can legislate). This division reflects the federal character of the Constitution and ensures a clear demarcation of authority between the two levels of government. The Union List has 100 subjects (now 97), the State List 61 (now 66), and the Concurrent List 52 subjects.

question: Which Act of the British Parliament provided for responsible government in the provinces? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (28/01/2021) Shift 1)

Act of 1909
Act of 1892
Act of 1935
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Act of 1935

Explanation:
The Government of India Act 1935, passed by the British Parliament, introduced responsible government in the provinces. It granted provincial autonomy, making the council of ministers responsible to the provincial legislature. This act abolished diarchy in the provinces and established a parliamentary form of government. The Act of 1935 was a landmark in the development of India's constitution and served as a blueprint for the future Constitution of India.

question: According to which article of the Constitution of India, it is the fundamental duty of every citizen to protect the natural environment? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (28/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: Article 51A
Article 55
Article 48A
Article 52
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 51A

Explanation:
The Fundamental Duties of Indian citizens are enshrined in Part IVA of the Constitution, added by the 42nd Amendment (1976). Article 51A (g) specifically states that it is the duty of every citizen to protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife, and to have compassion for all living creatures. This duty complements the Directive Principles and Fundamental Rights to ensure environmental protection. While Article 48A directs the State to protect the environment as a Directive Principle, Article 51A imposes a duty on citizens. Therefore, the correct answer is Article 51A.

question_hi: भारत के संविधान के किस अनुच्छेद के अनुसार प्राकृतिक पर्यावरण की रक्षा करना प्रत्येक नागरिक का मौलिक कर्तव्य है? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (28/01/2021) Shift 2)
